heading.purpose: One per hero card (e.g. "Scan to Add"); never a page-level title.

section-title.purpose: Label inside a bordered list card (e.g. "Recently Added").

row-title.purpose: Primary text of a list row or grid tile.

body.purpose: One-sentence supporting copy under a heading.

caption.purpose: Secondary line under a row title.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: The single elevation token — every card, tile, and CTA button, no variation.

shadows.name: header-seam
shadows.purpose: 1px hairline under a sticky header; deliberately not a blurred shadow.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Tap feedback on every interactive card/tile/button.

motion.name: sheet-spring
motion.purpose: Bottom confirmation sheets sliding up from y:100%.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one full-width pill CTA per screen (e.g. "Open Scanner").

components.description: The single card recipe — 16px radius, 1px neutral border, the one soft lift shadow.

components.name: List Row
components.description: A row inside the "More Tools"/"Recently Added" list-card pattern — icon-chip, title+caption, trailing chevron.

components.name: Compact Option Tile
components.description: A 2-up secondary-action grid tile, proportioned to match Settings' 3-column grid tiles rather than shrinking to its own text content.
components.css: .ds-option-tile { display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:space-between; width:100%; min-height:132px; padding:16px; background:#ffffff; border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:16px; box-shadow:0 2px 8px -4px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); text-align:left; cursor:pointer; transition:transform 0.2s, background 0.2s; } .ds-option-tile:active { transform:scale(0.95); background:#fafafa; } .ds-tile-top { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; width:100%; }

components.name: Sticky Search Header
components.description: The identity anchor for every mobile screen — a sticky, accent-colored bar holding the shared search field, in place of a page title.
components.css: .ds-sticky-header { position:sticky; top:0; z-index:20; background:#e27f2c; padding:12px 16px 8px; box-shadow:0 1px 0 0 #e27f2c; } .ds-search-pill { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; width:100%; height:40px; padding:0 12px; background:#ffffff; border-radius:12px; } .ds-search-icon { width:18px; height:18px; color:#9ca3af; flex-shrink:0; } .ds-search-input { border:none; outline:none; font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; font-size:14px; color:#1a1f36; width:100%; background:transparent; } .ds-search-input::placeholder { color:#9ca3af; }

components.name: Confirmation Sheet
components.description: A bottom slide-up sheet for anything that changes/discards state or needs a plain acknowledgement. Title and primary button echo the exact label that opened it; body is one sentence: 'Your {n} item(s) will {outcome}.' Icon tint signals intent (destructive vs. confirm); primary is a pill, secondary/cancel is rounded-2xl, never a pill.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-sheet-scrim { display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:flex-end; background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4); } .ds-sheet { background:#ffffff; border-radius:32px 32px 0 0; padding:24px; padding-bottom:calc(20px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); max-width:512px; margin:0 auto; width:100%; text-align:center; box-shadow:0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); } .ds-sheet-icon { width:48px; height:48px; border-radius:9999px; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; margin:0 auto 12px; } .ds-sheet-icon--confirm { background:#fff0eb; color:#e27f2c; } .ds-sheet-icon--destructive { background:#fef2f2; color:#ef4444; } .ds-sheet-title { font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; font-size:18px; font-weight:600; color:#1a1f36; margin:0 0 4px; } .ds-sheet-body { font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; font-size:13.5px; color:#6b7280; line-height:1.6; margin:0 0 24px; } .ds-sheet-cancel { width:100%; height:46px; margin-top:10px; border-radius:16px; border:1px solid #e5e7eb; background:#ffffff; color:#1a1f36; font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; font-size:14.5px; font-weight:500; cursor:pointer; }

narrative.overview:
Food Arca's dashboard is built for someone standing at a counter mid-shift, phone in one hand, a box of donations in the other. Every screen in this system reads like a clean, well-organized shelf: a small number of clearly-sized things, generous white space between groups, and photos doing the identification work that text would otherwise force someone to read under pressure. Nothing about it performs "software" — no dashboards-for-the-sake-of-dashboards, no dense data walls, no decorative flourishes. The system earns its calm by being genuinely restrained: one accent color, one shadow, one card radius, reused everywhere rather than reinvented per screen.

The reference implementations today are /dashboard/settings (the original polish benchmark), /dashboard/add's empty-cart state, its filled-cart state (the staged-items list), and its four confirmation sheets. Everything documented here was extracted from those implementations, not invented in the abstract — including two independent drifts (the filled-cart list's radius/shadow/borders, and the confirmation sheets' button shapes/icon tint/wording) that were caught and corrected after initially shipping out of step with the rest of the system.
keyCharacteristics: Photo-first recognition over text-first reading — a volunteer scans by image, not by label
One primary action per screen, unmistakably louder than everything else on it
Secondary/optional content is pushed away from the primary action with real vertical space, not just smaller type
A single soft shadow and a single card radius, reused without variation
No decorative chrome: no kickers, no gradients, no stat-filled empty states

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Exactly one warm color plays "the brand orange" on any given screen — reserved for the single primary CTA, the sticky header, and the active bottom-nav state.

rules.name: The Unconverged Orange Rule (open item)
rules.body: The codebase currently has two live values both claiming to be that one accent: #e27f2c (Add/scan flow) and #d97757 (Settings). Until a harmonization pass picks one, match whichever value the screen you're extending already uses.

rules.name: The One-Line Body Rule
rules.body: Supporting copy under a heading is one sentence. A second sentence belongs in a modal instead.

rules.name: No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No uppercase eyebrow/label ever sits above a heading.

rules.name: The No-Nested-dvh-Minimum Rule
rules.body: Never set a min-height in viewport units (100dvh) on an element already inside a scrollable flex container — it causes real iOS Safari scroll-clipping bugs. Use min-h-full instead.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a new component needs to feel lifted, it takes the exact Card Lift shadow value (0 2px 8px -4px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)). A second shadow recipe is a sign the component should probably just be a card.

rules.name: The One Quantity Rule
rules.body: A staged cart item's count appears exactly once per row, inside its stepper pill — never also restated as a separate 'N units' label. Weight-tracked items (no stepper) are the one exception.

rules.name: Mirror the Trigger Rule
rules.body: A confirmation sheet's title and primary button echo the exact label of whatever opened it ('Add to Inventory' button -> 'Add to Inventory?' sheet), and its body is one sentence: 'Your {n} item(s) will {outcome}.' Staged items are always 'your cart' in user-facing copy; 'batch' stays a code-only name.

dos: Do reuse the single Card Lift shadow and the single rounded-2xl card radius on every new card.
Do give every mobile screen a Sticky Search Header instead of a bold page title.
Do separate secondary/optional content from the primary action with a full section gap (24-40px), not just smaller type or a lighter color.
Do keep product/item photos in rounded-xl squares and system icons in rounded-full circles — the shape itself carries meaning.
Do use min-h-full, never a dvh-based min-height, on content nested inside an already-scrollable container.
Do make a confirmation sheet's title and primary button echo the exact label of whatever opened it, with one-sentence body copy: 'Your {n} item(s) will {outcome}.'
Do call the volunteer's staged items 'your cart' in every user-facing string.
donts: Don't add an uppercase eyebrow/kicker label above any heading.
Don't add a caption restating what a CTA obviously does.
Don't style a "view more"/tertiary link as a full-width, accent-colored button — that treatment belongs to the one primary CTA per screen only.
Don't introduce a third brand-orange value.
Don't mix a decorative rainbow of category colors into system iconography that's meant to read as neutral chrome.
Don't show a staged item's quantity twice on one row — the stepper is the single source of truth (weight-tracked items excepted).
Don't mix a centered scale-in modal into a screen whose other overlays are all bottom sheets.
